cells.tense: Something is in your hands right now, and its shape is still genuinely open.
cells.ask: Before the day fills, leave one thing unfinished on purpose. Take it from what you are already carrying and stop while it still has room to become.
cells.core:
Something is in your hands and the shape of it is still open. You're not deciding yet, and that isn't indecision — it's letting the thing stay available until the moment shows itself. Most people close a piece early just to feel settled, and the closing is where the life leaks out of it.

You can hold something loosely and stay in it at the same time, which is harder than it sounds. And when you lay a finished thing down, the ease in that isn't luck. You know the difference between work that is done and work you've stopped touching because finishing it would mean someone could see it. Keeping that difference is the practice.
cells.sheetLine: When something is finished, you let it go.
cells.verb: holding something open before it takes its final shape
cells.place: the threshold where work is finished and let go

cells.tense: Every version of the thing is still on the shelf, and you will get to them later than you keep telling yourself.
cells.ask: Choose one version you're holding and give it an end date. Write it down. Let the others sit without you; they aren't going anywhere.
cells.core:
You are holding every version of the thing at once — the one you could make of it, the one it might become, the one that would be truer later. Nothing has landed, and the waiting has started to feel like the work. It isn't. Each version you keep alive on the shelf is one you aren't living, and the shelf is getting crowded.

The one you picked has a better chance outside your head than inside it. Choose it, give it an end date, let the rest sit. You can return to a version you set down; a version you keep postponing stays a story instead of a thing. The light you'd shine from the finished piece is the light already in you.

cells.tense: There was a moment when this was open, and the closing has stood in for it since.
cells.ask: Describe one thing you've made to someone who wasn't there when you made it. Say what it was for and what it changed for you. Let their questions land.
cells.core:
What used to be open here has a wall in front of it now. You can feel where it went — a thing you made landed wrong once, and after that the making got careful. Careful isn't the same as finished. You've been building from behind something, and what you're guarding against is probably not in the room anymore.

What's low isn't the wanting. It's being seen in the middle of the work, not just at the end where it's safe, because a piece only closes when something outside you witnesses it. Say what you made and why it mattered, out loud, to one person. The wall is thinner than it looks from here.
cells.sheetLine: You went careful a while back and it hasn't lifted.

cells.tense: The doors are already there in the room you're standing in, and you keep describing the walls instead.
cells.ask: Name one choice you made today that you called something that happened to you. Then make one more, deliberately, the same way. A small one.
cells.core:
Choices are being made today, in the middle of the thing you're in, and they're getting filed as circumstances — what arrived, what came up, what had to get handled. You're steady about it and you carry it well. It just hasn't been called yours yet, and the calling is the part that's missing. The capability is not.

You don't need to see the whole situation to take the next step; enough light for one thing is enough. Name one thing a choice you made, then make one more the same way. Nothing about the day has to change for that to be true. It's already how you're living, and that part is settled.
cells.sheetLine: You're choosing all day. You're filing it as circumstances.
